column1: # Corpus for bin/fm-lint.sh's fixture-write purity check, read by
# It lives here rather than inline in that suite for the reason the check
# itself demonstrates: the check scans tests/*.sh, so a bypass spelling written
# as a literal in the suite IS a bypass site as far as the scanner can tell,
# and the suite would fail on its own test data. tests/assets/ is outside the
# scanned set, so the corpus can state each spelling exactly as a real suite
# Record format: <verdict> <TAB> <shell body>. A body may span several lines;
# \n in the body is expanded to a newline by the reader, so heredoc cases can
# state the opener, the body and the terminator that make them what they are.
# reject = the check must report this file and fm-lint.sh must exit non-zero.
# accept = the check must stay silent and fm-lint.sh must exit 0.
# --- the spellings the tree actually uses -----------------------------------
# --- a fixture bin/, where the tree symlinks the live repository's own bin/ --
# --- a variable naming a PATH shim directory that holds one tool -------------
# --- other file descriptors reach the same file through the same symlink -----
# --- the carrier's own forms, which is what the migration produced -----------
# --- a stub BODY is data the fixture writes, not a write the suite performs --
# --- and the rule must not reach past a fixture tool directory ---------------
